criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs sets planner_revision_effort stronger than the planner's effort and planner_timeout_s = 600. It runs a revision round (round 2) and asserts the planner AgentSpec timeout is greater than 600 s (1200 s). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The test `planner_revision_escalated_effort_scales_the_planner_time_limit` uses `repo_with_revision_keys(3, None, Some("xhigh"))`, whose planner effort is high and planner_timeout_s is 600. After a critic revise it asserts the efforts are high then xhigh, the timeouts are [600 s, 1200 s], `timeouts[1] > 600 s`, and the round-2 prompt contains 'deadline of 1200 seconds'. It checks the same for a mechanical revision. The timeouts are taken from `spec.timeout` on the AgentInvocation the fake agent receives. I ran it and it passed (1 passed). Athena's fails-without-1 run, with planning.rs reverted, exited 101.

criteria.criterion: A test asserts that round 1, and a revision with planner_revision_effort unset, weaker or equal, all keep exactly planner_timeout_s. Run: cargo test -p athena-core. The test fails if scaling is applied unconditionally.
criteria.evidence: The test `planner_time_limit_is_unchanged_when_the_revision_does_not_raise_the_effort` loops over the keys None, "medium" and "high". Each case makes three planner calls (round 1, a mechanical pass, then round 2) and asserts every timeout is exactly 600 s and every prompt says 'deadline of 600 seconds'. It passed in my run. Athena's fails-without-2 run passed with the fix reverted. That is expected: reverting removes the scaling altogether, so it cannot show what the criterion asks about. The test would still fail under unconditional scaling, because round 1 would be 1200 s against the asserted 600 s. It would also fail under scaling keyed only on `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`, because calls 2 and 3 would be 1200 s. I reasoned this from the code and did not run a mutant.

criteria.criterion: The diff in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs scales cfg.planner_timeout_s only when the revision setting raised the effort. It uses a named constant whose doc comment cites job 20261114-041123-hvyh (606 s against a 600 s limit at xhigh).
criteria.evidence: I read planning.rs lines 130-177 of the candidate. The timeout is multiplied only inside `if round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0` and then `if effort != base_effort`, using `saturating_mul(PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR)`. `timeout_s` feeds both `deadline_s` and `agent_spec`. The doc comment on `PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` (planning.rs:523-527) cites job 20261114-041123-hvyh, xhigh, 606 s against 600 s, and says the factor is an estimate.

findings.summary: Criterion 2's planned 'fails without' check (revert the fix) cannot show what that criterion asks about.
findings.evidence: Athena's fails-without-2 run passed with planning.rs reverted, because removing the scaling leaves every timeout at 600 s. The test does assert 600 s for round 1 and for the unset, weaker and equal cases, so it would fail under unconditional scaling. That conclusion comes from reading the code, not from a mutant run. The weakness is in the plan's demonstration, not in the test.

findings.summary: Escalation is inferred from string inequality, not from comparing effort ranks.
findings.evidence: `effort != base_effort` is correct only while `planner_revision_setting` returns a different effort solely when it ranks higher (config.rs:389-394, which holds today, and the comment says so). Comparing positions in EFFORT_LEVELS directly would not depend on that function's internals. The code is sound as written.

summary: I recommend accepting this change. It does what the retry asked: when a revision round raises the planner's effort above its own, `planning_round` doubles the planner's time limit using a named constant, `PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR = 2` (computed with `saturating_mul`). Every other call keeps `planner_timeout_s`. The agent and the planner brief's stated deadline receive the same number, and no other code reads `planner_timeout_s` to set a time limit. The check works because `Models::planner_revision_setting` (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:380-396) changes the effort only when the key ranks at least as high as the current effort and differs from it, which means only when it is strictly stronger. I ran both new tests and all ten `planner_`-filtered unit tests; they pass. Athena's run with the fix reverted showed the escalation test fails without it. Only the three expected files changed. The CHANGELOG entry cites job 20261114-041123-hvyh. The fmt, clippy and test results come from the CI run on this commit. The only findings are minor or nit, none of which blocks the change.
